title: t-J model at 50
abstract: I briefly overview the original formulation of the t-J model starting from Hubbard model, as well as stress its unique features, i.e., advantages and shortcomings when discussing its physical properties. Particular emphasis is put on a brief characterization of connection between magnetism, unconventional superconductivity, and the Mott-Hubbard localization of the correlated carriers in a narrow band. In the second part I summarize the model generalization to the three--orbital situation. The main purpose is to list some basic features of the physics associated with t--J model.
summary: This paper reviews the theoretical framework of the t-J model, detailing its derivation from the Hubbard model to explain high-temperature superconductivity. It emphasizes the crucial role of kinetic exchange interactions and extends the analysis to multi-orbital systems to address the charge-transfer nature of the superconducting gap in cuprates.
main_problem: The paper provides a comprehensive overview of the t-J model, aiming to characterize the fundamental physics linking magnetism, unconventional superconductivity, and Mott-Hubbard localization in correlated electron systems.
main_result: The t-J model effectively captures the physics of high-temperature superconductors by deriving an effective low-energy Hamiltonian from the Hubbard model via perturbation theory.
method: The derivation relies on canonical perturbation expansions, systematically projecting the Hubbard model onto subspaces that exclude high-energy doubly occupied states.
model_or_system: The primary model is the t-J model, derived from the Hubbard model, and extended to three-orbital systems relevant for cuprates. The Hamiltonian involves hopping integrals (t), on-site repulsion (U), and exchange couplings (J).
key_observables: Superconductivity (d-wave pairing), antiferromagnetism, charge gap mechanism, and the nature of the charge carrier (d-character vs. itinerant).
important_parameters: The ratio of hopping energy to on-site repulsion ($t/U$) is the crucial small parameter governing the effective low-energy physics.
main_assumptions: The derivation assumes that the on-site repulsion $U$ is the largest energy scale ($U \gg |t_{ij}|$), allowing for a systematic expansion in powers of $t/U$.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates various hopping processes, including virtual, real, and three-site hopping, used in the derivation of the effective Hamiltonian.
paper_structure: The paper first reviews the derivation of the t-J model from the Hubbard model in real-space and k-space, detailing the role of kinetic exchange. It then generalizes the model to three-orbital systems, discussing the transition from a Mott-Hubbard gap to a charge-transfer gap.
why_interesting: The detailed theoretical mapping from the Hubbard model to the t-J model, and the subsequent extension to three-band models, provides a foundational framework for understanding strongly correlated phenomena relevant to advanced quantum materials.
